plan.working_title: EloraTZP in Type 2 Diabetes: What's Confirmed? #shorts
plan.why: It follows up our biggest earner (44% of long-form watch time), and 'eloralintide' and 'eloratzp' are our proven search terms. It also feeds that long video's views back in while its daily minutes are slipping. | fact-check: The figures check out (top dose 23.3% weight loss and 2.9-point A1C drop at 48 weeks, adults with obesity or overweight and type 2 diabetes, Phase 2b NCT06603571, Lilly-reported). But the framing is wrong in two ways. (1) This isn't new ObesityWeek data. The results were first released around 1–2 Oct 2026 (EASD 2026; Lilly release, Healio 2 Oct, Medscape). ObesityWeek was a re-presentation, so calling it 'new' breaks the craft rule against calling older data new. (2) The trial DID have a randomized tirzepatide-alone arm: tirzepatide 15 mg gave 14.8% weight loss and a 2.4-point A1C drop, against 23.3% and 2.9 for the top EloraTZP dose. So the planned 'no tirzepatide-alone comparison' fallback would be false. Also check that the 10-01 'Did EloraTZP Beat Tirzepatide?' long-form isn't about this same trial. If it is, the Short must still add one new fact (for example the A1C result, or the share reaching normal blood sugar if the primary release prints it).

We answer one tirzepatide question from the research every day. Subscribe if that helps. Full breakdown on our channel, link in the description. (Post note for the owner: set the related-video link to the 10-01 EloraTZP long video. The spoken word count is still 160 after the s5 fix, using the shorter prescriber line the fact-checker allows. The full line would make it 168. The s5 discontinuation figure is now 'stopped because of side effects', with the 2.9% tirzepatide-alone comparator on screen. factcheck.summary: I checked every number, the trial description and the mechanism wording against Lilly's 30 Sep 2026 press release (src1, which loads). They all match. The 23.3% vs 14.8% weight loss and the −2.9 vs −2.4 A1C points come from the top combination arm (eloralintide 9 mg + tirzepatide 15 mg) against tirzepatide 15 mg alone, at 48 weeks. The trial was randomized and enrolled 367 adults with obesity or overweight and type 2 diabetes. These are efficacy-estimand results, which the release defines as "had all randomized participants remained on study intervention", so "if people stayed on treatment" is correct. Stopping because of side effects ran 10.8–27.0% on EloraTZP (27.0% on the top arm) vs 2.9% on tirzepatide alone. Side effects were mostly stomach-related. Eloralintide is a selective amylin receptor agonist and tirzepatide a dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist. EloraTZP is investigational; the release only says Phase 3 is planned. The Short is framed honestly: it names one company-reported trial, shows the comparator in every stat, scopes the population and is clear that EloraTZP isn't approved. The safety lines are there. I count 160 spoken words, which is at the limit. The shortened prescriber line fits an unapproved drug. One optional precision fix is below.
